notes: SHIP v1.14.397 - M1-a: BACKUP COVERAGE IS DERIVED, NOT REMEMBERED. First data-safety ship of the blueprint program, and the precondition for everything that follows: nothing else in the reconstruction touches storage until a backup can actually round-trip. THE DEFECT (audit 04 ST7). exportAllData hand-listed FIFTEEN named sections. The app has roughly 63 keys. Sixteen of the uncaptured ones are real field work - per-node field-verify status, discrepancies, deploy issues, audit walks, the scan collection, optic score history, classifier overrides, checklist state, power topology. A technician could tap EXPORT FULL BACKUP, migrate device, restore, and silently lose a third of their shift. A backup that omits user data is worse than no backup, because it is trusted. THE FIX. A registry, PHANTOM_BACKUP_EXTRA_KEYS, with one row per key and a stated reason, plus a prefix sweep for dynamically-named keys (phantom_scaffold_v1::*). Export emits every registry key verbatim under bundle.keys. Restore pushes them into the SAME _writes array the named sections use, so they inherit the existing snapshot, the headroom pre-check and the full transactional rollback for free - the restore path was already the best-built thing in the storage layer and this ship reuses it rather than replacing it. Named sections WIN on collision, deliberately: they carry referential-integrity filtering that drops orphan racks and phases against valid deployment ids, which a verbatim copy would bypass. The rule going forward is that a key which exists is in the backup unless it has a row saying why not, and 13 keys have such a row: ephemeral probes, session and device-local UI state, the PIN LOCKOUT (restoring a lockout would lock a freshly restored device), the crash log, backup metadata about the backup itself, three dead keys, and Ghost Echo quirks which travel separately under ID-DEDUP MERGE semantics that a verbatim overwrite would destroy. SCHEMA STAYS AT 1, DELIBERATELY. bundle.keys is additive and ignorable. Bumping the schema would make an older cached build REFUSE this bundle outright via its _bs guard, instead of best-effort restoring the named sections - and a degraded restore beats a refusal in the field. To keep that honest in the other direction, the restore confirmation now states up front when a file PREDATES the registry and therefore cannot contain field-verify status, discrepancies, deploy issues, audit walks or the scan collection, and otherwise reports how many additional keys it carries. No silent partial restore. VERIFIED BEFORE SHIP: all 25 registry keys are referenced elsewhere in the app (no invented keys), no duplicates. NOTE ON THE BUILD ITSELF: the first cut of this ship failed node --check with Unexpected token else - the anchor line for the user-facing warning was the head of an if/else-if chain and the insert orphaned the else. Caught by the compile gate before push, which is what the gate is for. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, CSS braces 4557/4557, line endings preserved, three-stamp lockstep. STILL TO COME IN M1: safeGet and safeRemove (neither exists today, so all 121 getItem and all 31 removeItem calls are raw), phantom_node_status_v1 routed through safeStore, the two unguarded BOM setItem calls, ge_load read-modify-write, the corrupt-data quarantine path, and precaching pdf.min.js. DEVICE-VERIFY: with a real deployment loaded, EXPORT FULL BACKUP and confirm the downloaded JSON contains a keys object; open it and confirm phantom_node_status_v1 is present if you have field-verify status on this device.
